terms.meaning: A marker in the template that the build step replaces with real data.
A small store inside the user's browser that keeps settings between visits.
The part of a web address after the # sign, used here to decide which view to show.
Converting characters such as angle brackets into safe text so they show instead of being run as page code.
A named colour or size value reused across the page's styling rules.
A typeface downloaded from the internet when the page loads.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Page head, theme and first styles
sections.what: Sets up the page's title, the calm and nerd colour and font sets, and the basic styling. A short script at the top applies the saved mode before the page appears, so the page does not flash the wrong look.
sections.why: The mode is applied before the first paint so the page does not flash, and the saved mode key is shared with the portfolio site.
sections.watch_out: Only the exact value nerd switches to the nerd look, so any other saved value falls back to calm.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Top bar and sidebar styling
sections.what: Styles the sticky top bar with its breadcrumb trail and mode switch, and the two-column layout with a fixed-height sidebar. It also styles the area and file list in the sidebar.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The sidebar is fixed to the window height, so long file lists scroll inside the sidebar rather than the whole page.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Styles for headings and the mind map
sections.what: Styles the page headings, the summary text and the mind map boxes, lines and labels, including the open, dimmed and focused states of each box.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: File setup (part 4)
sections.title: Styles for notes, code rows and badges
sections.what: Styles the fact lists, term lists, warning banners, the two-column code and note rows, the status badges, the checks table and the collapsible skipped-files list.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: File setup (part 5)
sections.title: Small-screen rules and page layout markup
sections.what: Adjusts the layout for narrow screens and print, and turns off animation for users who ask for reduced motion. The markup then lays out the skip link, top bar, sidebar with search and view links, and main area. It also holds the data placeholder and opens the page script.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, though reduced motion support follows a common accessibility setting.
sections.watch_out: The data placeholder is replaced only by the build step, so opening this template directly shows the empty state.

sections.name: File setup (part 6)
sections.title: Mode switching and empty-state guard
sections.what: Handles clicks on the mode button and saves the choice to the shared key. It also checks that the embedded data loaded, and if not, shows an empty-page message and stops the rest of the script.
sections.why: The saved key is shared with the portfolio so the owner's choice carries across the site.
sections.watch_out: If the embedded data is missing or cannot be read, the whole page stops at this point and shows only the empty message.

sections.name: File setup (part 7)
sections.title: Helper functions and breadcrumb links
sections.what: Provides small helpers that make text safe to display, format backticks as code, shorten long text, split file paths, build links and badges, and mark each file as explained or not. It also builds the breadcrumb trail back to the portfolio and the links to GitHub line ranges.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the links it builds to the portfolio and to GitHub.
sections.watch_out: Text is made safe before backticks are turned into code, so any HTML written in a note shows as plain text.

sections.name: File setup (part 8)
sections.title: Grouping files into areas and counting
sections.what: Groups files into their areas, sorting areas and placing files that have no known area into a catch-all group. It sorts files with the start-here list first, then by size, and counts the totals for the overview and the readiness stats.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the grouping it creates for the sidebar and the mind map.
sections.watch_out: A file whose area name is missing from the repository's area list gets its own group, so a misspelled area shows up as a separate group.

sections.name: File setup (part 9)
sections.title: Search and sidebar file tree
sections.what: Filters the file list by name, summary and terms as the owner types, then redraws the sidebar tree with each file's status dot. Enter opens the first match, and the slash key moves the cursor into the search box.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the search behaviour it provides.
sections.watch_out: Enter opens the first visible match, which may not be the file the owner meant, so the search should be checked before pressing Enter.

sections.name: File setup (part 10)
sections.title: Drawing the mind map layout
sections.what: Calculates where each area box and file box goes on the mind map, decides which area is open, and draws the map as an image with lines joining the root, the areas and the open area's files.
sections.why: Likely reason: it gives a visual summary of how the parts fit together, as the page's hint text describes.
sections.watch_out: Only the first 14 files of an open area are drawn, and the rest appear as a more-files box that links to the area page.

sections.name: File setup (part 11)
sections.title: Map clicks, keys and detail panel
sections.what: Handles clicks and the Enter and Space keys on map boxes, so an area opens or closes, a file opens its page, or the more-files box opens the area page. It also fills the detail panel beside the map with the area's name and summary.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the navigation it provides from the map.
sections.watch_out: Map boxes respond only to clicks and the Enter and Space keys, so any new interactive element needs the same keyboard handling.

sections.name: File setup (part 12)
sections.title: Overview and area pages
sections.what: Builds the overview with the repository's headline, summary, audience, run instructions, coverage counts, the mind map, the start-here list and the list of skipped files. It also builds each area page with its reasons and its file list.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the sections it presents to the owner.
sections.watch_out: Opening an area the notes do not list shows a does-not-exist message rather than an error.

sections.name: File setup (part 13)
sections.title: Single file page with code and notes
sections.what: Builds a file's page: a banner if the code has changed or some of it is unexplained, a plain-English summary with its facts, the terms it uses, and then one row per section pairing the numbered code lines with its note.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the reading experience it creates: code on the left, notes on the right.
sections.watch_out: Code lines that belong to no section never appear on the page, even though the page text says every line belongs to a row.

sections.name: File setup (part 14)
sections.title: Readiness, decisions and debugging pages
sections.what: Builds three of the site's pages. The readiness page shows a table of twelve checks and lists the files that are not ready or need work. The decisions page lists recorded choices with their reasons and alternatives. The debugging page shows a fixed method for finding bugs and a list of known problems.
sections.why: Likely reason: each page is built in the browser from data stored inside this one file, so the notes work without a server.
sections.watch_out: The readiness lists only show files marked not-ready or needs-work, so a file with status ready or unknown never appears there.

sections.name: File setup (part 15)
sections.title: Glossary page, not-found text and router start
sections.what: Builds the glossary by merging project-wide terms with the terms each file declares, then adds a live search box. It also builds the plain not-found message and the first part of the router, which chooses the page to show from the web address.
sections.why: Likely reason: merging terms means each word appears once, with links to the files that use it.
sections.watch_out: When two sources define the same term, only the first meaning is kept and the later one is silently dropped.

sections.name: File setup (part 16)
sections.title: Scrolling and first page load
sections.what: After a page is drawn, scrolls to the section named in the web address, or back to the top. It also reacts when the address changes and draws the first page when the file opens.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page has no server, so the address after the hash symbol is the only way to link to a specific section.

summary: A single HTML page template that the build step fills with a repository's plain-English notes and code, so the owner can browse each file with a note beside every section.
purpose: Gives the owner a browsable explanation of the repository, including an overview, a mind map, search, file pages and readiness results, that works offline in any browser.
why: Likely reason: one self-contained file can be opened directly or published on the portfolio without a server. The reason for the calm and nerd looks is not stated in the code beyond its styling.
how: The build step puts the repository data and title into the template. On load, the page picks the saved mode, reads the data, groups files into areas, counts progress, and draws the sidebar and mind map. The page address decides which view is shown: overview, area or file. A file page pairs each section's code lines with its note.
inputs: The data that the build step writes into the page, the mode choice saved in the browser, and the owner's clicks, search text and page address.
outputs: A page in the browser. It saves the chosen mode in the browser's local storage and writes no files.
risks: Notes can be out of date when the code has changed, and the page shows them as written. The page loads fonts from an outside service, so its look changes when offline.
debug: If the page says it is empty, the data was not inserted, so rebuild with the build command. If a file page shows wrong notes, check the banner about changed code and rebuild. For layout problems, check the mode setting and the browser's error console. Only the first 13 parts of this file were visible, so views such as readiness, decisions, debug and glossary were not checked.
